boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Arizona, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe sequence of campus landmarks, a study stop, and optional scheduled activities for a first Tucson weekend.

cards.title: Start at Old Main
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · historic campus core
cards.notes: Begin with a slow lap around the wraparound porch and grounds, then use the building’s interpretive history to orient yourself to the original campus.
cards.short_summary: See the university’s oldest building and a central historic landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Main is the University of Arizona’s oldest building; it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972.
cards.source_title: Historic Preservation at the University of Arizona
cards.access_notes: The university’s Spirit & Traditions page describes Old Main as having a wraparound porch with rocking chairs.

cards.title: Pause at Berger Memorial Fountain
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · immediately west of Old Main
cards.notes: Stop at the octagonal fountain before continuing across campus; read its memorial purpose and keep the visit respectful of the people it commemorates.
cards.short_summary: A named historic fountain beside Old Main with a documented memorial purpose.
cards.evidence_claim: Berger Memorial Fountain, immediately west of Old Main, memorializes UA students who died in World War I and was dedicated in 1920.
cards.source_title: Historic Preservation at the University of Arizona
cards.access_notes: Located immediately west of Old Main, according to the university preservation page.

cards.title: Walk through Krutch Garden
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · east of Old Main on the Campus Mall
cards.notes: Follow the paths and pause at the distinctive boojum and Sonoran native plants; use the garden page as a lightweight plant-identification guide.
cards.short_summary: A historic Campus Mall garden featuring Sonoran native plants.
cards.evidence_claim: The Joseph Wood Krutch Garden stands east of Old Main and includes Sonoran native plants, including cactus species and a boojum tree.
cards.access_notes: The garden page describes shaded seating and a self-guided tour option; stay on established paths around plantings.

cards.title: Choose a self-guided arboretum tour
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus-wide walking activity
cards.notes: Pick the Arboretum History, Edible Landscapes, Sonoran Native Plants, or Medicinal Plants booklet and make a short route that fits your energy.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, campus-wide way to notice named trees and gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Campus Arboretum offers self-guided tour booklets that direct visitors to campus locations with described trees.
cards.access_notes: Tour options and available booklets are listed by the UA Campus Arboretum; confirm any current tour logistics before setting out.

cards.title: Regroup at the Student Union Memorial Center
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 1303 E. University Blvd.
cards.notes: Use the building as a practical reset point: locate student services, check event postings, and meet up before choosing your next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building that houses student-focused services and event spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Union Memorial Center is at the heart of campus and hosts services including Meal Plans, CatCard, and the Basic Needs Center.
cards.access_notes: Address: 1303 E. University Blvd. Check individual services or events for current availability.

cards.title: Find the U.S.S. Arizona Bell
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Student Union Memorial Center tower
cards.notes: While at the Union, look up toward the bell tower and read the memorial context; the bell is preserved in the tower as a dedicated memorial.
cards.short_summary: A documented historic bell preserved in the Student Union tower.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Union preserves one of two original bells salvaged from the U.S.S. Arizona; it is dedicated to those who died on the battleship.
cards.access_notes: The bell is preserved in the Student Unions tower; view it as part of the building rather than treating it as a separate public program.

cards.title: Make a Main Library plan
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · 1510 E. University Blvd.
cards.notes: Take a floor-by-floor look, choose a quiet or group-study area for a future session, and note the Tech Toolshed and CATalyst Studios.
cards.short_summary: A flexible study and creation stop with quiet floors and technology services.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Library provides study, collaboration, technology, and research spaces, including quiet study rooms and CATalyst Studios.
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary by date; check the library’s current hours page before going.

cards.title: Add Flandrau to the afternoon
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · 1601 E. University Blvd.
cards.notes: Check the day’s program before heading over, then allow time to explore the science-center and planetarium visit at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: A campus science center and planetarium with published visitor hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Flandrau Science Center & Planetarium is located at 1601 E. University Blvd. and lists Tuesday–Sunday visitor hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Hours and Parking | Flandrau Science Center & Planetarium
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; the page says admission must be purchased, so confirm current programming and tickets.

cards.title: Try a beginner bouldering workshop
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · SouthREC
cards.notes: Check the current workshop schedule, wear closed-toe shoes, and start with the staff-led introduction rather than attempting advanced moves on your own.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Campus Recreation climbing activity with beginner-friendly instruction.
cards.evidence_claim: Outdoor Recreation offers weekly bouldering workshops, and its FAQ says no prior climbing experience is needed for climbing workshops.
cards.access_notes: Workshops are regularly scheduled but can be canceled; closed-toe shoes are required in the bouldering area. Check the current schedule and access requirements.

cards.title: Learn the Bear Down story
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · campus spirit tradition
cards.notes: Before a game or campus event, read the university’s account of the motto and listen for it in context rather than assuming a particular event is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A documented University of Arizona rallying cry with a specific campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: “Bear Down!” became the University of Arizona rallying cry after student body president and quarterback John Byrd “Button” Salmon’s 1926 final message to his coach.
cards.access_notes: This is a campus tradition rather than a guaranteed scheduled event; consult official Athletics or campus calendars for current events.
